name: Russia–NATO
value: Missiles, drone entered Polish airspace 20 Nov
summary: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone entered its airspace on 20 Nov, a 'provocation'; no Article 4 found
state: Poland's defence minister said three objects, likely two missiles including a Kh-101 and a jet-powered drone, entered eastern Polish airspace overnight into 20 Nov, and Prime Minister Tusk called it an intentional Russian provocation (RTE; The Moscow Times). Poland said it would ask NATO for more support on the eastern flank. On 20 Nov Denmark said it would expel Russia's defence attaché over an alleged Russian plot to kill a rapper (Euronews). No Article 4 request or direct clash was found as of 21 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Air travel and rail in eastern Poland and the Baltics can see short disruptions after incursions. People travelling to the region can check FCDO travel advice for the latest guidance.
rubric_hit: Watch: airspace violations by Russian missiles and a drone over Poland (20 Nov); no Article 4 or attack declared

sources.title: The Moscow Times — Poland condemns Russian 'provocation' after 3 airspace violations

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
